title: Housing minister defends Labour’s policy record at committee
summary:
Housing Minister Matthew Pennycook has defended the Government's housing policy record during questioning by MPs, rejecting claims that Labour lacked a comprehensive plan when entering office in 2024. The minister cited a 15% increase in new-build starts but declined to confirm progress towards the 1.5 million homes target.

title: Five million UK households to face higher mortgage costs
summary:
More than five million UK households are expected to face higher mortgage repayments when they refinance over the next two years, according to the Bank of England's latest Financial Stability Report. The Bank estimates that just over five million borrowers will see their monthly repayments rise by the end of 2028, an increase from its previous projection of nearly four million.

title: Property sellers expect agent responses within 24 hours
summary:
Estate agents face mounting pressure to respond to client communications within 24 hours across nearly all stages of the property sales process, according to new research from Street Group. A survey of 1,830 current and recent home sellers found that rapid response times have become a key factor in agent selection.

title: Student lettings face disruption from Renters’ Rights Act
summary:
The student lettings sector is experiencing significant disruption following implementation of the Renters' Rights Act, with landlords and agents facing unexpected financial losses this summer. Early termination provisions have resulted in void periods that could eliminate annual profit margins for many operators.

title: World Cup and warm weather slow UK housing activity
summary:
The UK housing market has experienced a temporary slowdown in recent weeks, with Purplebricks chief executive Michael Bruce attributing the pause to the World Cup and warm weather conditions. The Lloyds house price index showed average property prices reached £299,330 in June, up 0.2% from May.

title: Reeds Rains opens Hull branch after Kaye’s acquisition
summary:
Reeds Rains has completed the rebranding and reopening of its Newland branch in Hull following the acquisition of Kaye's Estate Agents. The transaction includes the transfer of a fully managed lettings portfolio to the new branch.

title: Oxford conference to address AI and marketing in agencies
summary:
A conference examining artificial intelligence, marketing and industry trends in the estate and letting agency sector will take place at the University of Oxford on 20 November. The Voice of the Agent Conference follows the publication of 12 research reports during 2026 covering agency fees, marketing, AI, recruitment, regulation and consumer behaviour.

title: Senior property professionals join brokerages and franchises
summary:
Three established property professionals have taken up new roles across the residential sector, signalling continued structural shifts in the industry towards brokerage and franchise models. The appointments include a former Hamptons director joining Moveli and a property management firm opening a Manchester office.

title: Property cooling costs rise as heatwaves prompt retrofit
summary:
UK homeowners are investing in cooling measures as recurring heatwaves challenge traditional property design, with external shading systems emerging as a cost-effective alternative to air conditioning units. External shading can reject up to three times more solar heat than internal blinds, according to industry experts.

title: Bridging lender completes £2.475m Kensington penthouse deal
summary:
Specialist bridging lender Aspen has completed a £2.475 million Bridge-to-Let facility for a four-bedroom Kensington penthouse, marking its second prime central London deal within seven days. The property was acquired at auction by a foreign national investing through a Spanish-registered corporate entity.
